sam.role: engineer (someone who designs and builds things to solve problems)

case.title: The Beacon Went Dark
case.hook: The light at the end of the Palmetto Beach jetty (a rock wall that sticks out into the water) went dark. Boats use it to find the harbor at night. Nobody plugs it in. So where does its energy come from?

notice.head: NOTICE TO MARINERS · PALMETTO BEACH
notice.title: JETTY LIGHT OUT
rows: The green light at the end of the jetty is not working.
Use extra care entering the harbor at night.
notice.line: Mariners (people who drive boats) read notices like this one.

ticket.head: Keeper’s work ticket
ticket.title: Jetty light: checked this morning
rows: Works when I test it with a spare battery
Covered in a white crust. Our pelican loves to sit on it!
ticket.foot: Sam, can you figure out what went wrong? ~ the harbor keeper

stills.alt: A real photo: two Coast Guard crew members in hard hats install a small light with a solar panel on top onto a red marker in the water.

case.stillsCredit: U.S. Coast Guard crew installing a solar-powered LED light on Lake Erie: photo by Petty Officer 3rd Class George Degener, U.S. Coast Guard (public domain, via Wikimedia Commons).
case.question: The jetty light’s lamp still works. So why did the light go dark?
case.how: Find 4 clues as you work through the lesson. Then crack the case (solve it) at the top of the Assignment tab.

clues.t: Every device takes energy IN and sends energy OUT in a different form. A device can only change the energy it gets.

clues.where: The Lesson, Part 1: flip the arrow tag
clues.t: The jetty light’s solar panel CHANGES light into electrical energy, and its lamp CHANGES electrical energy back into light.

clues.where: The Lesson, Part 2: the energy pipes
clues.t: A device never makes energy and never uses it up: 10 units in, 10 units out. With 0 units in, you get 0 out. A battery only stores energy that came in.

clues.where: The Lesson, Part 3: back to the Sun
clues.t: Follow the energy back far enough and it almost always starts at the Sun. The jetty light’s chain starts with sunlight hitting its panel.

solve.title: Why did the jetty light go dark?
solve.q: Which answer fits all four clues?

options.t: The LED lamp used up all its light.
options.why: Check Clue 3. Energy doesn’t get used up, and the ticket says the lamp still works.
Check Clue 3. A battery never makes energy. It only stores energy that came IN.

options.t: The crust on the panel blocked the sunlight. No light went in, so no electrical energy was made, the battery emptied, and the lamp had nothing to convert.
options.why: Case cracked! No energy in means no energy out. The chain broke at the very first step: sunlight couldn’t reach the panel. Fill in Sam’s repair ticket just below.

options.t: Nights are too dark for a light to work.
options.why: Check Clue 4. The light works at night on energy the panel collected during the day.

blackbox.title: The black box
todo: Read what goes IN and what comes OUT.
Drag the device that fits onto the box (or tap the card, then the box).

why.t: Something you can’t see inside. You only see what goes in and what comes out, and you can still figure out a lot!

reveal.alt: A real photo looking down into a running toaster: a slice of bread sits over glowing orange wires.
reveal.line: Electrical energy IN. Heat OUT (useful: it toasts the bread), plus a little light and a click.

reveal.alt: A real photo of an electric desk fan with dark blades behind a wire cage.
reveal.line: Electrical energy IN. Motion OUT (useful: the spinning blades push air), plus a hum and a little heat.

reveal.alt: A real photo of a solar garden light on a metal stake, with a small dark solar panel on its round top.
reveal.line: Light IN by day. Its little panel changes it into electrical energy, a battery stores it, and at night the lamp changes it back into light. The jetty light works the same way.

a.fan: A fan makes moving air. Does Box A make wind?
a.solar: Box A’s input is a wall plug, not sunlight.
a.flash: A flashlight runs on batteries, and it makes light, not LOTS of heat.

b.toaster: A toaster makes lots of heat. Box B makes moving air.
b.solar: Box B’s input is a wall plug, not sunlight.
b.flash: A flashlight makes light. Box B makes moving air.

c.toaster: A toaster needs a wall plug. Box C’s input is sunlight.
c.fan: A fan needs a wall plug and makes moving air.
c.flash: Close! But a flashlight’s energy comes from batteries you put in. Box C’s comes from the Sun.

blackbox.q: What did every box do to the energy that went in?

opts.t: It changed the energy into a different form.

opts.miss: Could the fan run if you unplugged it? Where did its energy come from?

opts.t: It kept the energy exactly the same.
opts.miss: Electricity went into the toaster. Did electricity come out?

blackbox.win: Energy IN, a different form OUT. Every device is an energy changer. Clue 1!

arrowtags.afterText: A flashlight converts electrical energy INTO light
arrowtags.title: Flip the arrow tag
todo: Tag each arrow MOVES or CHANGES: drag a tag onto it, or tap the arrow to flip it.

why.t: MOVES = transferred: same form, it just travels. CHANGES = transformed: a new form.

arrowtags.noneLine: Tag at least one arrow first: MOVES or CHANGES.

scenes.why: Motion in, motion out. The energy MOVED from one marble to the other.
scenes.miss: The first marble was rolling. What does the second marble do? Is that a new form?

scenes.why: Electrical in, heat out. The energy CHANGED form.
scenes.miss: Electricity went in. Does electricity come out, or something else?

scenes.why: Sound traveled through the air to your ear. Same form: it MOVED.
scenes.miss: The drum made sound. What reaches your ear? Is that a new form?

scenes.why: Electrical in, motion out. The energy CHANGED form.
scenes.miss: Electricity went in. Spinning blades are what kind of energy?

scenes.why: Light in, electrical out. The panel CHANGED the form. That’s the jetty light’s first step!
scenes.miss: Light hits the panel. What goes out of the panel on its wires?

scenes.why: Electrical in, light out. The lamp CHANGED it back into light.
scenes.miss: The battery sends electricity. What comes out of the lamp?

opts.t: The fan: electrical energy turns into motion.
The marbles: motion passes to another marble.
opts.miss: Did the form change, or did motion just move to the other marble?

opts.t: The drum: sound travels to your ear.
opts.miss: Sound went in and sound arrived. Did the form change?

arrowtags.win: MOVES keeps the form. CHANGES makes a new form. The jetty light changes energy twice! Clue 2!

pipes.afterText: Test it with the energy pipes
pipes.title: The energy pipes
todo: Pick a device and drag the slider to guess.
Press Pour and count both pipes. Try 3 devices, including both bulbs.

why.t: A pretend scoop of energy, so we can count it. Sam’s numbers are about right for real devices.

pipes.guessQ: Guess first: of {n} units, how many come out USEFUL?

xtra.t: heat in the air, glow, click

devices.note: Most of it becomes heat, but not all of that heat goes into the bread. Some warms the kitchen air.
An old-style bulb turns only about 1 of every 10 units into light. The rest becomes heat. That’s why old bulbs get so hot!
An LED turns much more of its energy into light, so it needs much less energy for the same brightness.
A gas car turns only about 2 of every 10 units into motion. Most becomes heat in the engine.
A solar panel turns about 2 of every 10 units of sunlight into electrical energy. The rest warms the panel or bounces off.

pipes.needLine: Try at least 3 devices, including the old bulb and the LED bulb.
pipes.q: 10 units of energy went into the old bulb. How many units came out?

opts.miss: The heat came out too! Count every unit in both pipes.

opts.t: 0, because the bulb used it all up.
opts.miss: Look at your pipe log. Did the units disappear, or come out in a new form?

pipes.win: Nothing used up, nothing made: 10 in, 10 out, every time. So 0 in means 0 out! Clue 3!

trace.title: Follow it back to the Sun
todo: Start with the hot toast. Each right answer takes one step backward.
Keep going until the trail can’t step back any more. Then follow 1 more device.

why.t: Every device gets its energy from somewhere. Going backward shows where it started.

trace.empty: 👆 Pick a device to start your trail.
trace.arrowNote: The arrows show which way the energy moved: from the start to your device.

foods.name: Hot toast

steps.q: The toast got its heat from the toaster. Where did the toaster get its energy?

opts.miss: The bread got hot, but bread doesn’t power the toaster. What does the toaster plug into?
Devices can’t make energy (Clue 3!). What goes INTO a toaster?

steps.q: Where did the electricity in the wires come from?

opts.miss: There’s no battery in your wall. The wires run a long way, to a big building.
Lightning is electrical, but nobody catches it to run toasters. Where do the power lines lead?

steps.q: Most of Florida’s electricity comes from power plants that burn natural gas. Where did natural gas come from?

opts.t: 🦠 Tiny sea living things, buried for millions of years

opts.miss: People pump natural gas from deep underground. What turned into gas down there?
Natural gas is pumped from deep underground, not from the air.

steps.q: Those tiny sea living things needed energy to grow. Where did it come from?

opts.miss: Waves moved them around, but many of them made their own food, like plants do. What do plants use?

opts.t: ☀️ Sunlight: they made food from it, like plants

opts.miss: Sand has no food energy. What do plant-like living things use to make food?

foods.end: Your toast’s heat started as sunlight, millions of years ago! It was stored in tiny sea living things, then natural gas, then turned into electricity, then heat.

foods.name: A ceiling fan

steps.q: Where does the fan get its energy?

opts.miss: The fan MAKES moving air. What does it plug into?
A fan’s motor has magnets, but they don’t make energy. What goes INTO the fan?

steps.q: This fan’s home has solar panels on the roof. Where did the panels get their energy?

opts.miss: Rain can make panels dirty! What do solar panels change into electricity?
Heat actually makes panels work a little worse. What lands on a panel?

foods.end: Sunlight to panel to wires to fan: a short chain, and it still starts at the Sun.

foods.name: You, riding a bike

steps.q: Your legs push the pedals. Where do your muscles get their energy?

opts.miss: Sleep helps you rest, but it doesn’t give your body energy to use. What do you eat?
The bike gets its motion from YOU. Where does your energy come from?

steps.q: Cereal is made from grain, like wheat or corn. Where did those plants get their energy?

opts.miss: Plants take in water and minerals from soil, but their energy comes from somewhere else. Look up!
Plants need water, but water has no food energy. What else do plants need?

foods.end: Sunlight to wheat to cereal to your muscles to the bike. YOU are an energy changer, too!

foods.name: The jetty light

steps.q: At night, where does the jetty light’s lamp get its energy?

opts.miss: Moonlight is much too dim to power a lamp. What is stored inside the light?
The waves splash the jetty, but nothing catches their energy here. Look at the keeper’s ticket.

steps.q: The battery only stores energy. Where did its energy come from?

opts.t: 🔲 The solar panel, during the day

opts.miss: A battery can’t make energy (Clue 3). What fills it up each day?
The lamp USES the battery’s energy. What fills the battery?

steps.q: And the solar panel got its energy from…

opts.miss: The pelican only blocks the panel! What should be landing on it?
Salt spray just makes the crust worse. What should reach the panel?

foods.end: Sun to panel to battery to lamp. If sunlight can’t reach the panel, the whole chain breaks!

twist.head: Almost every chain starts at the Sun!
twist.t: Food, natural gas, oil, wind and solar power all trace back to sunlight. A few don’t: nuclear power plants (Florida has some) and the heat deep inside Earth start somewhere else.

trace.q: What did every chain you followed have in common?

opts.t: It started at a power plant.
opts.miss: Look at the left end of your trails. Was there a power plant in the bike chain?
Look at the left end of your trails. What is always there?

trace.win: From the Sun to your toast! The jetty light’s chain starts with sunlight on its panel, too. Clue 4!

repair.kicker: Case closed · fill in the repair ticket
repair.title: Sam’s repair ticket
todo: Tap the link in the jetty light’s chain that broke.
repair.lockLine: Crack the case first. Then fill in the repair ticket.
repair.brokenQ: 1. Tap the link where the chain broke.

brokenMiss.sun: The Sun was shining every day. Something stopped the light from getting IN.
brokenMiss.battery: The battery was empty, but why? Nothing was filling it.
brokenMiss.lamp: The ticket says the lamp works with a spare battery.
brokenMiss.boats: The boats are fine. They just can’t see a light!

repair.brokenLine: The panel! Salt crust and pelican droppings blocked the sunlight, so the panel couldn’t change light into electrical energy.

fixes.t: Clean the panel, and put a perch post next to it for the pelican.

fixes.miss: A brighter lamp still gets 0 units in. Fix the first link!
Two empty batteries are still empty. What needs to fill them?

ticket.head: Repair ticket
rows: Light couldn’t get into the solar panel.
Panel charged the battery all day. Lamp on all night.

repair.win: FIXED! The jetty light shines green again, and the pelican has its own perch.

harbor.kicker: Bonus game · unlocked after the case
harbor.title: Light the harbor
todo: Pick the device you think fits best.
Can you get 3 stars on every job?
harbor.lockLine: Crack the case first. Then this game opens.

jobs.t: Light the dock path all night. There are no wires out there.

picks.line: Perfect: no wires, and they charge themselves every sunny day.
They work, but someone has to change the batteries all the time.
Mostly heat, a tiny glow, and it needs a wall plug. Not a light!

jobs.t: Warn boats on a foggy night, when lights are hard to see.

picks.line: Sound travels through fog, so boats hear it even when they can’t see.
It helps a little, but thick fog blocks light.
Moving air won’t warn a boat far away.

jobs.t: Keep the keeper’s radio working through a cloudy, stormy week.

picks.line: Turn the crank: your own motion powers it, sun or no sun.
Great on sunny days, but a cloudy week gives it very little energy.
Warm, but it can’t run a radio, and the rain puts it out.

harbor.win: 9 stars! You matched each job to the right energy change. Next lesson, you design a device of your own.

harbor.tease: Three night jobs at the harbor. Pick the best device for each, and earn 3 stars.

tool.name: Plug-in watt meter
tool.teaser: Plug in a lamp, a fan, a toaster and more. How much energy goes IN?
tool.done: You measured every device. A watt meter sticker is in your Field Notebook.

why.q: What does a watt meter do?
why.t: You plug it into the wall, then plug a device into it. Its screen shows how fast the device takes in electrical energy, in units called watts (W).

wattmeter.title: How much energy goes IN?
todo: Tap a device to plug it into the meter.
Read the watts on the screen.
Plug in all 6. Your watt bars build themselves.
wattmeter.ladderLabel: Watts going IN (more watts = energy goes in faster)
wattmeter.pairLine: The old bulb and the LED make about the SAME amount of light. The old bulb needs about 60 watts. The LED needs about 9!

loads.note: A small trickle: electrical energy IN, stored in the phone’s battery.
Bright light for only a few watts, because less of its energy turns into heat.
Electrical IN, motion OUT (plus a hum and a little heat).
The same brightness as the LED, but much more energy goes in, and most of it comes out as heat.
Electrical IN, light and sound OUT (and some heat out the back).
Huge! Making heat fast takes lots of energy. Never touch a toaster’s wires.

q.q: The old bulb and the LED make the same light. Why does the old bulb need so many more watts?

opts.t: Most of its energy comes out as heat instead of light.
opts.why: Right! The LED wastes less as heat, so it needs much less energy for the same light.
They make about the same light. Where does the rest of the old bulb’s energy go?

opts.t: It uses up the energy faster.
opts.why: Energy doesn’t get used up. It changes form. What form, besides light?

q1.A: Think about the energy pipes: 10 units in, 10 units out. Did anything get used up?
q1.C: That’s energy moving (transfer). What’s different about conversion?

q2.A: The turbine’s blades turn a machine inside it. What kind of energy goes out on its wires?
q2.B: A little heat comes out, but that’s extra. What’s the useful output?

q3.B: What did the toaster’s owner want: toast or a click?
q3.C: The input is what goes IN. Is the click going in or coming out?

cer-4.re: because|so |this shows|that shows|this means|that means|which means|proves|since

What went IN? What came out USEFUL? What else came out?

ans-2: Transfer = energy moves. Transformation = energy changes form.
Think about the arrow tags: the marbles and the fan.

hlCoach.title: Highlight like a scientist
tips: Highlight key words, not whole paragraphs.
If everything is yellow, nothing stands out. Aim for a few words in each paragraph.
Look for words that are explained.
Bold words, and words followed by “means”, “is called” or a meaning in ( ), are often worth saving.
Look for answers to the Big Question.
Ask yourself: does this help me explain how energy changes from one form into another?
“Because”, “so” and “first … then” show how ideas connect.
Yellow = important. Green = evidence I might use in my answer. Pink = something I wonder about.

practice.q: Practice: tap the 3 to 5 words that matter most in this sentence.
practice.text: A device converts the energy that goes in into a different form, and the energy is never used up.
practice.model: A scientist might highlight “device converts”, “different form” and “never used up”. Those words hold the big idea. Small words like “a” and “the” don’t carry the idea.

hlCoach.outside: This works in every subject. When you read anything, save the words that answer your question, and skip the rest.
